newsitem.title: FRANCE: Moulinex sees 1997/98 operating profit rise.
newsitem.headline: Moulinex sees 1997/98 operating profit rise.

text.p: French appliance manufacturer Moulinex said on Wednesday it expected a significant rise in operating profit and return on capital for the 1997/98 year.

"The year 1997/98 begun in a difficult European spending environment should be a new phase. The board expects a significant recovery in operating profit and in return on capital," Moulinex said in its 1996/97 earnings statement.

"If you look at the conditions under which the first year of the (three-year restructuring) plan was launched ... even in a difficult sales environment, I expect a significant rise in the operating result for 1997/98," Chairman Pierre Blayau said.

Moulinex reported net attributable profit of 29 million francs ($5 million) for the 1996/97 year ended on March 31, its first full-year profit since 1991. It had a 702 million franc loss for 1995/96 after taking a 600 million restructuring charge.
Its operating profit rose to 160 million francs in 1996/97 from 54 million in the preceding year.
Blayau told Reuters there was no plan to add further restructuring provisions in the current-year accounts. ($ = 5.823 French Francs)
